newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Tuesday on an uncertian short-term market trend, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended at 3,322 yuan ($400) per tonne, losing 28 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 3,323 and hit a low of 3,321.
January rose seven to 3,244 yuan per tonne, March fell 13 to 3,237, May 101 to 3,379, July rose 33 to 3,383 and September 10 to 3,380.
Combined volume rose to 6,500 tonnes from 4,300.
Traders said profit-taking pushed some contracts down slightly but most contract moved in a narrow range due to an uncertain short-term market trend.
"Given a lack of market-moving news, the market is having a hard time attracting speculators, resulting in dull trading," one trader said.
Analysts expect soybean to remain stable in the short term.
